chunks: It has been narrated: “Concerning one who finds a fish and does not know whether it is of that which may be eaten or not, then the base of its tail should be split. If it turns toward greenness, then it is of that which may not be eaten; and if it turns toward redness, then it is of that which may be eaten.

And if a snake swallows a fish and then throws it out while it is still alive and wriggling, then if its scales have peeled off, it should not be eaten; and if its scales have not peeled off, it may be eaten.”

key_terms.أَصْلُ ذَنَبِهِ: the base of its tail; the place mentioned for testing the fish
key_terms.الْحُمْرَةِ: redness; a sign indicating the fish may be eaten
key_terms.الْخُضْرَةِ: greenness; a sign indicating the fish is not to be eaten
key_terms.تَسَلَّخَتْ: peeled off; the condition of the scales that makes the fish impermissible
key_terms.حَيَّةٌ: snake; the creature that swallows and expels the fish
key_terms.سَمَكًا: fish; the animal whose edibility is being evaluated
key_terms.فُلُوسُهَا: its scales; the feature affecting the ruling after expulsion
key_terms.يُؤْكَلُ: may be eaten; legally permissible for consumption

ai.seo_question: How can one determine if an unknown fish is halal to eat in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives fiqh-based indicators for determining whether a fish is halal (permissible) to eat when its status is uncertain. It also clarifies the ruling for a fish expelled by a snake, making the condition of its scales relevant to permissibility.
